name: Corporate Clean
reads_as: Calm, modern corporate: light cool field, deep navy ink, one confident blue for the thing being named, amber for terms, teal for outcomes, slate for context, geometric grotesk type, flat rounded cards with soft shadows, a faint dot grid.
_notes: Token roles, measured contrast pairs and the polish checklist live in the guide (s2, s13). 2026-10-07 polish: caption_active is light amber #FCD34D (7.98:1 on the pill; accent2 was 2.29:1, the RC20 tint #D6A078 5.02:1); accent3 pink #DB2777 became slate #64748B (the runtime uses accent3 as the default context bar, book, pot, pointer pill and calendar colour, so pink leaked into frames the pack never meant it for); accent4 and pos #0D9488 became #0F766E (white text on the old teal was 3.74:1, so teal tags printed white at 3.74:1 and teal boxes got navy icons while every other accent got white); people wear ink, not the accent; the fx mesh is blue-only at 0.2 (at 0.55 with pink and teal, muted text fell to 3.71:1 on its blue pole). The label floor stays 24 px: raising it to 26 made Loom.ui artefacts overflow (lab_ui_artefacts '09:16' and a preview line, preview harness); bespoke labels are set at 28 to 30 px by the guide instead.

captions._active_note: caption_active is a caption-only token: light amber, 7.98:1 on the pill composited over the field, and a clear hue step from the white words. Never use it in scene art (1.34:1 on the field).

characters._cloth_note: People wear navy by default so a person never takes the accent's job (the blue marks what the narration names). Background people wear muted, line and surface2 (runtime/scenery.js crowd), so the cast reads one value step above the crowd. A second cast member takes top: accent3 (slate) or muted, never accent, accent2, pos or neg.
characters._extras_note: what a background person is (D-100): people = the cast's rigs in muted clothes; silhouette = the grey bean; none = no crowd. Change it here, never per lesson.

join_note: Plain and quick: a cut between topics is right; continue inside a topic; covers (dip, fade, wipe, iris) only at a section change, if at all.

fx._mesh_note: Blue-only and quiet: a pole tints the field at most 12 % toward the accent (#DBE5F9), where muted text holds 5.02:1. The old blue, teal and pink mesh at 0.55 tinted 33 % (#B0C6F6, muted 3.71:1) and read as a pastel gradient behind slides (feedback-that-lands, lab_fx). A lesson that wants a dead-flat field sets storyboard fx.enabled false.
fx._grain_note: D-100: grain is off or near-off by default; per-pixel noise reads as grit after H.264 on a 1080p MP4 (L-173). A lesson may set storyboard fx.grain to choose a film finish.

materials._decor_note: 2026-10-08 (L-276), from guide s2: set decorations and default object tones are not the point, so they take accent3 (context and neutral objects: context bars, iso boxes that are not the point) instead of accent (the named thing only), accent2 (type and one pill, never a data series) or accent4 and pos (they read as correct). Cables add line (connectors); the envelope is surface (anything you could pick up or read); the document is accent3 because a surface document draws its header in the accent. Left at the runtime default because s2 allows it: vessel, calendar and heart accent3, phone surface2. The laptop reads no tone.
